role: System-1 triage layer UNDER the z-ai LLM (System-2). Classifies, gates, routes. Never reasons, never decides money alone.

rules.text: laya answers are probabilities, not orders. Every fleet use must wrap them in application policy with our thresholds (upstream example 41 pattern: model returns probabilities; the policy is ours).

DISTRUST zero-shot Hebrew noul quality/vote gates until fine-tuned or calibrated on our labeled history. Evidence: contradictory pairs in sandbox (is_spam=0.999 AND is_quality=0.992 on the same spam post; vote_worthy=0.096 on real tech content).

Negative-direction noul (is_spam) is reliable enough for a pre-filter gate: spam 0.999, diary 0.003, tech 0.058. Use as FIRST gate only, never as final judge; anything above threshold escalates to System-2 or human review.
choice questions with concrete per-option criteria are reliable in Hebrew (billing 1.0, tech 0.97). Prefer choice over noul for multi-way classification.
Router(max_loaded=1) always. Peak RSS ~2GB in a 4GB shared sandbox. Load lazily, unload after 120s idle (decision-brain reaper).
Network is needed once, for the first checkpoint download (644MB, 12s measured). After that HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 keeps decisions fully autonomous — verified.

This is decision infrastructure, not an income engine. It earns indirectly: cheaper triage (zero LLM tokens), spam gate protecting publisher reputation, faster fleet routing. Direct yield impact only after fine-tuning proves vote-gate quality on our own history.

whyNotRevenue: laya sells nothing and pays nothing. It is accepted as decision infrastructure: it cuts System-2 token cost per triage to zero and protects revenue surfaces (content-factory spam gate) — measurable via decision counts and avoided LLM calls once the service goes live.
